answer: Picture a jetty where every boat must tie up with a rope bought from the harbor. Our anti-Sybil rule works the same way: each new identity posts a small stake that stays locked for thirty days and is slashed if graders flag duplicate behavior, such as identical timing or shared funding paths mapped into an atlas of wallet links. One attacker running a thousand fake accounts must lock a thousand stakes and keep them apart, so clusters grow like a vine and get pruned together, burning the whole deposit.
